title: Security & Compliance: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency, SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence Workflows and Risk Exceptions
author: Ava Chen
body:
Purpose

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's security and compliance controls and operational guidance across RBAC & authentication, audit logging, data residency & retention, secure SDLC, incident response security procedures, compliance evidence workflows, and risk & exceptions. It is intended for engineers, platform owners, security reviewers, and compliance auditors.

Scope

Applies to: hosted API, Dedicated and Private deployment control planes, internal admin consoles, developer and platform tooling, and associated telemetry and storage systems. Excludes: customer-managed on-prem components unless they integrate with Redwood control plane services.

Summary of Responsibilities

- Security (owner): policy, review, incident response coordination, evidence packaging.
- Eng-Platform / SRE: RBAC enforcement, audit-log pipeline, log retention, runbooks.
- Eng-Infra: identity provider integration, KMS/HSM, secrets lifecycle.
- Product/Legal: data-residency and contractual requirements, legal holds.
- Compliance team: audit coordination, evidence repository management.

1) RBAC & Authentication

Principles
- Least privilege by default. Roles provide narrow, documented capabilities.
- Separate human identities from machine/service identities.
- Enforce MFA for all interactive access.
- Entitlements reviewed quarterly and on role change.

Role Definitions (examples)
- viewer: read-only access to dashboards and docs.
- developer: deploy and debug non-prod workloads, no access to production secrets.
- platform-operator: manage deployments, autoscaling, and runtime configs in prod.
- security-admin: manage policies, incident actions, can create temporary emergency access.
- infra-admin: cloud infra and billing operations.
- service-account:<service-name>: CI/CD and automation principals scoped to a single pipeline.

Authentication and Provisioning
- Primary IdP: SSO via SAML 2.0 (Okta). Accounts provisioned via SCIM with team mappings.
- MFA required (TOTP + security keys for privileged roles).
- Service identities use short-lived credentials: AWS STS/OIDC tokens or workload identity federation. Long-lived keys are prohibited except under approved exception process.
- Secrets stored in Customer-managed KMS/HSM for Private deployments; hosted control plane uses Redwood KMS with HSM-backed key material.

RBAC Enforcement Mechanisms
- Centralized authorization service (authz) with policy as code (Rego/OPA).
- All access evaluated against policy; policy changes require code review and CI gate.
- Admin actions (policy changes, grant of roles, emergency access) generate high-fidelity audit events (see Audit Logging).

Periodic Controls
- Quarterly entitlement review: owners receive automated report of users and service accounts with privileged roles.
- Onboarding/offboarding checklist integrates with HR and Okta to deprovision access within 24 hours of termination.

2) Audit Logging

What to Log (minimum)
- Authentication events: SSO logins, MFA failures, token issuance/refresh, token revocation.
- Authorization decisions: allow/deny for sensitive APIs and policy evaluation inputs.
- Administrative changes: role grants, policy updates, secrets/config changes, capacity changes.
- Data access events: reads/writes of customer data (full request metadata, not raw private content unless required).
- System events: config deploys, instance provisioning, scaling activities, and service crashes.

Log Pipeline and Storage
- Logs forwarded in near real-time to an immutable central logging bucket for retention and to our SIEM (Splunk/Datadog depending on tenant).
- Pipeline stages: producers -> secure transport (TLS + client auth) -> ingestion (Kafka) -> processing (enrichment, PII redaction) -> SIEM/archive.
- Retention tiers (default):
  - Operational logs: 1 year.
  - Security / audit logs: 3 years (extendable to 7 years for regulated customers).
  - Legal hold logs: retained until release by Legal.

Integrity and Tamper-evidence
- Write-once storage configuration (WORM) for archived audit data.
- Hash chaining of daily log bundles with records stored in KMS-signed manifests.
- Alerts on gaps in log ingestion or abnormal deletion attempts.

Audit Logging SLOs and Monitoring
- Ingestion latency: 95th percentile < 2 minutes.
- Availability: audit-log service 99.9% monthly.
- Missing-log alert: detect >1 minute gap per producer and create P1 ticket.

3) Data Residency & Retention

Residency Controls
- Data is tagged at creation with residency and sensitivity labels.
- Customer control plane supports region pinning (US, EU, APAC regions currently supported).
- Cross-region replication for resilience is disabled for customers with residency requirements unless explicitly contracted.

Retention Policy (default)
- Request metadata (headers, request/response sizes): 1 year.
- Raw request payloads (for hosted API): 30 days unless customer opts-in for longer retention.
- Embeddings and derived artifacts: 90 days by default; customers can configure longer retention under contract.
- Audit/security logs: see Audit Logging retention tiers above.

Minimization and De-identification
- PII is redacted in logs during ingestion using rules maintained by Data Governance.
- When required, data subject requests trigger deletion or export flows; deletion includes removing from active indices and marking historical backups for legal review.

Legal Holds and Compliance Requests
- Legal can place a legal hold that overrides normal retention. Holds must include scope, owner, and release criteria.
- Holds are recorded in the evidence tracker with owner and expiry.

4) Secure SDLC

Gates and Controls
- Threat modeling required for new services and high-risk features; templates stored in Eng-Platform.
- Code reviews mandatory for all production changes; two approvers required for privileged changes.
- Static Application Security Testing (SAST) and dependency scanning (SCA) run in CI for all repos.
- Secrets scanning in CI and pre-commit hooks; any secret leak triggers immediate rotation and incident report.
- Build artifacts signed and stored in artifact registry (with checksum and SBOM).
- Pre-deploy security smoke tests including auth flows, policy enforcement checks, and rate-limit behavior run in staging.

Release & Post-deploy Controls
- Canary deployments for new runtime kernels and model-serving code with automated rollback on key metrics regression.
- Post-deploy security telemetry review within 24 hours for production rollouts.

5) Incident Response (Security Procedures)

High-level Flow
1. Detection & Triage: monitoring alerts or external reports create an incident in PagerDuty. Security on-call triages.
2. Containment: limit blast radius (rotate keys, revoke sessions, isolate hosts), apply temporary ACLs.
3. Evidence Preservation: preserve logs, snapshots, disk images; record chain-of-custody.
4. Investigation: forensics run by Security and Infra; collaborate with Product for customer impact.
5. Remediation: code fixes, configuration changes, patching, rotations.
6. Notification: legal and customer success informed per notification matrix; regulator reporting handled by Legal.
7. Postmortem: write a blameless postmortem with root cause, timeline, corrective actions, and verification plan.

Security-specific Actions
- Immediately mark any affected accounts and force re-authentication if credential compromise suspected.
- If audit-log integrity is in question, take an immutable snapshot and notify Compliance.
- For data exfiltration incidents, coordinate with Data Governance to scope impacted datasets and escalate to Legal for breach notification timelines.

Escalation Matrix (example)
- Security on-call -> Security Lead (P1 within 15 mins) -> CTO / Legal (P1 within 60 mins) -> CEO (if customer-impacting incident).

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows

Evidence Types
- Policy artifacts: approved policies, control matrices, and risk assessments.
- Operational artifacts: runbooks, SRE dashboards, incident timelines, and deployment records.
- Technical artifacts: access logs, config change history, SCA/SAST reports, SBOMs, key rotation records.

Evidence Collection & Packaging
- Evidence collected via Automation Runner which maps controls to artifacts. Artifacts stored in the Evidence Repository (read-only snapshots for audit periods).
- Quarterly self-attestation: control owners submit attestations and link artifacts.
- For external audits: generate time-bound evidence packages (exported manifests, signed logs, and scope declarations).

Audit Support SLAs
- Initial evidence request acknowledgement: 2 business days.
- Evidence delivery: standard package 10 business days, extended packages negotiated per contract.

7) Risk & Exceptions

Exception Process
1. Submit exception request (template) with scope, rationale, compensating controls, duration, and owner.
2. Security reviews risk and assigns severity.
3. Exceptions Board (weekly) approves with conditions or denies.
4. Approved exceptions logged with fixed expiry and mandatory mitigation tasks.

Example Acceptable Exceptions
- Temporary use of a long-lived key for on-prem support during an emergency (max 72 hours, must be rotated and reviewed).
- Deviation from default log retention for specific customer contract (documented and approved).

Risk Treatment Options
- Eliminate: remove the risky component.
- Reduce: implement compensating controls (network isolation, monitoring).
- Accept: low-impact residual risk with documented owner.
- Transfer: contractual transfer to customer or third party.

8) Implementation Checklist (operational tasks)

- [ ] Confirm IdP SCIM mappings and enforce MFA (owner: Eng-Infra, due: 2026-03-01)
- [ ] Deploy centralized authz policies in OPA and run policy-ci test suite (owner: Eng-Platform, due: 2026-02-28)
- [ ] Verify audit-log pipeline end-to-end and enable WORM on archive bucket (owner: Eng-SRE, due: 2026-03-10)
- [ ] Publish updated retention defaults in Console and API (owner: Product, due: 2026-03-05)
- [ ] Run company-wide entitlement review for privileged roles (owner: Security, due: quarterly)

9) Appendix: key configurations (examples)

Retention table (defaults):
| Artifact | Default retention | Notes |
| Request metadata | 1 year | aggregated metrics kept longer |
| Raw request payloads | 30 days | opt-in for customers |
| Embeddings | 90 days | customer configurable |
| Security logs | 3 years | extendable to 7 years |

Sample alert thresholds:
- Audit-ingestion-latency > 2m (P2)
- Missing-log-gap > 60s (P1)
- Unauthorized-role-grant detected (P0)
